en.title: Wayfair OA #2: Number of Divisible Substrings
en.description: Map lowercase letters using this fixed table: ab→1, cde→2, fgh→3, ijk→4, lmn→5, opq→6, rst→7, uvw→8, xyz→9. Count the contiguous non-empty substrings whose sum of mapped values is divisible by the substring length. Count by position: identical content at different positions is counted separately. The mapping image in the fixed original text was a broken local path; this site restored it from the public Problem Source original image on the original FastPrep page, and the original starter also explicitly references LC2950; the evidence and image hash are in the editorial.
en.input: A lowercase English string word, without quotes. Full original range 1≤word.length≤2000; the empty string is not accepted.
en.output: Output the number of qualifying contiguous non-empty substrings, as an exact integer with no modulo.
en.explanation: Original examples kept: asdf→6, corresponding to a, s, d, f, as, sdf; bdh→4, corresponding to b, d, h, bdh; abcd→6, corresponding to a, b, c, d, ab, cd. The first group ab has only two letters, so you cannot map by three letters per group or by a phone keypad.
hints: Divisibility is equivalent to the substring's average mapped value being an integer.
The possible integer averages are only 1 to 9.
After fixing the average k, subtract k and count substrings with zero sum.
